sections.title: Why this module matters
sections.body: PostgreSQL interview questions go beyond generic SQL — MVCC and the PostgreSQL transaction model, JSONB indexing strategies, partitioning (declarative + inheritance), the rich window-function vocabulary, replication (streaming + logical), backup and PITR strategy, query planning with EXPLAIN ANALYZE, and the Spring Boot + HikariCP tuning patterns that surface in real interviews. This page is the one to use when the job description specifies Postgres (which is most of them in 2026).

sections.title: Mental model
sections.body:
Postgres = **relational core + power-user extras**.

- **MVCC** — readers don't block writers; vacuum reclaims dead tuples.
- **JSONB** — first-class document storage, indexable with GIN.
- **Window functions, CTEs, recursive queries** — keep complex logic in SQL.
- **Partitioning** — declarative since 10; range, list, hash.
- **Replication** — streaming (physical) + logical (selective tables).

sections.title: Must-know concepts
sections.body:
The interview surface for this module breaks into these focus areas:

- **Postgresql features** — drill the named patterns, the failure modes, and the recommended Java / framework idiom.

sections.title: Likely interview hooks
sections.body:
- **VACUUM** is mandatory — long transactions block it; bloat kills performance.
- **JSONB indexing** — GIN with `jsonb_ops` vs `jsonb_path_ops`.
- **`SERIAL` vs `IDENTITY`** — IDENTITY is the modern, spec-compliant default.
- **`SELECT FOR UPDATE SKIP LOCKED`** — the classic queue-in-Postgres pattern.
- **Hot standby** — read-only replica; mention `pg_basebackup` and `walsender`.

sections.title: Speaking template
sections.body: > *"For Postgres I'd lean on <JSONB | partitioning | window function> because <fit-for-feature>, watch for <bloat | replication lag>, and tune <work_mem | shared_buffers | autovacuum> for the workload before reaching for sharding."*
